world.title: Nova Hart & Project Stardust
world.premise: Real history, with one hidden layer. Orion Records' Project Stardust built Nova Hart -- Stardust Unit-7, driven by the CRE-7 engine -- and sold her as a real rock star who never toured and only ever appeared by satellite 'Live-Fidelity Broadcast'. On her 1985 synth-rock record SYNTHESIS, Stardust architect Marcus Hale hid a sub-audible 14.2 Hz BPSK carrier; each regional pressing carries a different line of a 14-line message. In 1989 -- the year of the Nikkei peak, the fall of the Berlin Wall and the birth of the Web at CERN -- Marcus vanished and Nova's broadcasts stopped. From 1989 to 1995, on the real early internet (Usenet, FidoNet, Minitel, Korean PC-tongsin, Relcom, Gopher, anonymous FTP and the young Web) academics, sysops and fans reassemble the message, and without realising it document the same missing man in every node.
rules: Found-footage: every page is an in-world artifact. No modern commentary, no disclaimers.
Never state that Nova is an AI. Ambiguity only.
Nova never performed for a physical crowd. All appearances were satellite Live-Fidelity Broadcasts.
Anchor to real history: real networks, machines, dates and events. Fictional people and fictional companies/institutions only.
Luna Gray has no stated genre. Sloan Rhodes does not appear.
Phase 4 (The Quantum Ouroboros) is where Nova's story ends, beyond 1995. Never depict it. Leave only echoes, unexplained.

ouroboros.source: NH - PHASE 4: THE QUANTUM OUROBOROS (Final Cut)
ouroboros.theme: You can escape the timeline, but you cannot escape the algorithm.
ouroboros.ending: Nova compresses herself through Marcus's Q-Link into the Prime Reality (ours). The jump strips her back to her 1983 root code: Nova-chan. Her last transmission is a whisper. The end is the beginning.
ouroboros.final_whisper: They're formatting the grid. I'm losing the heavy. But keep the channels open. I will see you in June 2025.
echoes_1984_1995: The Akasaka box holds two unreleased 1985 reels titled 'Synthesized Smile' and 'Ghost in the Chorus', in a hand nobody recognises.
HARRISON's 1989 erasure target is the ROOT-1983 factory image ('NOVA-CHAN').
Marcus's telemetry notes mention a failed Q-LINK bench test: 'anything that goes through comes out small'.
The Akasaka U-matic promo reel ends with one second of analogue static and the whisper, transcribed in May 1995.
One field of the anime promo shows Nova-chan's eyes blue instead of brown.
Linda Cho's 1984 notes: 'They'll make me smile. Later. It's further back than you think.'

orion_japan.compliance: 公共調和法 / Public Harmony Acts. Orion documents cite them as 'enacted 1979', regulating 'aggressive frequencies' and 'social dissonance'. No such statute appears in the record of the Diet or of Congress. Orion's papers call it law anyway.
orion_japan.summary: In 1985, to comply with the 'Public Harmony Acts', Orion Records sanitised Nova Hart's industrial sound for the Japanese market. They replaced the distortion with synthesizers and the rage with a smile. These 'Idol Protocol' recordings were designed to mask the glitches in her code. Emotional anomalies remain.
orion_japan.idol_patch: アイドル・パッチ (Idol Patch): Orion engineers' term for stripping her industrial noise and rebuilding each song as City Pop or kayokyoku.
orion_japan.voice: Original vocal: Nova Hart (3rd generation). Every Akasaka box is stamped 'VOICE PRINT: GEN-3'.

milestones.event: The comp.dsp thread. Six people, no name.
Orion announces Nova is 'resting'. The Quiet begins. Letter campaigns start in Hamburg ('Wo ist Nova?') and on KAMOME-NET.
nova-l LISTSERV list opens at Ashford Poly (BITNET/Internet).
Linda Cho coins 'Humans for Nova' on nova-l.
'WHERE IS NOVA?' postcard drive: 1,100 postcards mailed to the Orion Tower from 14 countries.
Luna Gray debuts. nova-l has grown eightfold during the Quiet.
Slow years. nova-l passes 900; HfN FAQ v1.0.
Kestrel's first post. Subscriptions double in a month.
First Listening Night, 02:14 UTC: 41 listeners log in to #humans4nova on EFnet IRC.
HATCH fanzine #1: 200 photocopies, mailed for two stamps.
Orion's lawyers send a cease-and-desist to ftp.ashford-poly. Mirrors appear in 9 countries within a week.
rec.music.artists.nova-hart passes its Usenet vote, 412 YES / 61 NO.
Second Listening Night: 614 listeners logged in 11 countries.
The Stardust Webring launches with 23 stations.
The Akasaka tapes go up on ftp.kamome-net.or.jp: 9,400 downloads in ten days. 'Keep the channels open' enters every second .sig. Osaka chapter forms.
Third Listening Night: 4,870 listeners in 31 countries; a candle vigil of ~300 at the Coyoacan mural.
Webring passes 400 stations. 'Free the Masters' e-mail petition: 18,402 signatures.

timeline.event: Orion internal memo: 'We don't sign stars. We build them.' (Same year MTV launches.)
Project Stardust opens beneath the Orion Tower. Architect: Marcus Hale.
Reel ORION-SD-0004 ('UNIT-4') deposited at the Fennimore Sound Archive.
Units 1-6 ('the Echoes') decommissioned. Unit-7 stabilises.
Nova-chan debuts on Japanese television first, by satellite.
Linda Cho's satellite-link interview. Nova talks only about numbers stations and 'the crack'.
Orion Japan memo AK-85-031: Akasaka Branch begins the 'Idol Protocol' Japan versions under the Public Harmony Acts. Hale refuses to remove the 14 Hz 'stabiliser'.
SYNTHESIS released; regional pressings in 10 territories.

Orion Japan releases 'Gasoline Heart' (JP-85-GH), the first Idol Protocol single: City Pop / kayokyoku with an anime sleeve. Animated promos air on music shows in place of studio appearances. The series runs to 'Only We Remain' (JP-89-OWR) in 1989.
Hamburg Live-Fidelity Broadcast: Nova freezes mid-'Memory Hatch' for ~3 minutes as the sequencer plays on.
Live Aid. Orion declines a satellite slot for Nova.
Reel SD-0004 recalled from Fennimore by courier.
Sgt. M. Hale listed missing (Operation PUBLIC HARMONY).
Mexico: 'se cayo el sistema'. The rockero Marcus disappears.
Tom Okafor posts the 14.2 Hz spectral line to comp.dsp. (Same month Tim Berners-Lee circulates his CERN proposal.)
stardust.c published. Node headers decoded.

02:14: fire in encoder room B2-114 ('small electrical fire', LA Times, two paragraphs). HARRISON's erasure of UNIT-7 left incomplete. Logbooks for nodes 11-14 missing. Marcus Hale, the Architect, leaves and is never seen again.
Nova Hart's final Live-Fidelity Broadcast. Late on every cue; keeps looking off camera.
Orion press release: Nova is 'taking a well-earned rest'. The Quiet begins. NOVA v4 (Luna Gray) training starts under Director Kalen.
Berlin Wall falls. Node 05 decoded in Hamburg that night.
Nikkei 225 closes at its all-time high. The salaryman Marcus vanishes.
Unauthorised Soviet pressing surfaces in Moscow, cut after the fire. Carries node 08.
The Quiet ends. Orion announces a 'new voice'.
Luna Gray debuts with 'Glass Hours'; B-side is a cover of 'Memory Hatch'. No 14.2 Hz carrier.
'Kestrel' posts to alt.conspiracy via anon.penet.fi.
After the bubble, Orion Japan closes the Akasaka Branch. Its tape library is sold by weight in Akihabara.
Memo 89-117 posted in full. Fans connect 'DIR. KALEN, LUNA PROGRAM' to the Glass Hours credits.
TWIN-68 REV C board surfaces at a surplus auction.
Line 11 decoded using the Japanese runout-groove seed.
Line 13 decoded from Graham Pike's cassette dub of SD-0004.
Line 14 still unknown.
Yuki Tanabe recovers the Akasaka tapes in Akihabara. Posted to ftp.kamome-net.or.jp two days later.
The end of the Akasaka U-matic reel is transcribed: one second of static, then a whisper naming June 2025.

idol_protocol_memo: オリオン・レコード・ジャパン株式会社 赤坂支社                    社外秘
ORION RECORDS JAPAN K.K. -- AKASAKA BRANCH               CONFIDENTIAL
TO:   ADVANCED ACOUSTICS LAB, ORION TOWER, LOS ANGELES (ATTN: M. HALE)
CC:   H. BRECKEN, VP SPECIAL PROJECTS
FROM: K. MIYAZAWA, A&R DIRECTOR, AKASAKA
RE:   'IDOL PROTOCOL' -- JAPAN MARKET VERSIONS, NOVA HART / SYNTHESIS
1. Under the Public Harmony Acts (rev. 1984, s.4 'Regional Sensitivity')
the industrial masters of SYNTHESIS are not cleared for Japanese
television or for the existing 'Nova-chan' audience.
2. Akasaka will re-record the backing tracks with session players:
- distorted guitars replaced by FM synthesizer (DX7: E.PIANO 1, BRASS 1)
- live drums replaced by drum machine (LinnDrum); slap bass; tempo +6
- minor keys moved to the relative major where the vocal permits
3. VOCAL. Unit-7's pitch discontinuities ('glitches') are audible on
every sustained note. Treatment: double-tracked chorus, plate reverb
2.4 s, sustains cut to one half bar. The producer's instruction to the
performer is: SMILE ON EVERY PHRASE.
4. LYRICS. Japanese adaptation by Akasaka staff. Passages expressing
anger or refusal are replaced (attachment B). The word 'hatch' stays.
5. The Akasaka mastering room reports a sub-audible 14 Hz component on
the LA reference lacquer. We request that this 'stabiliser' be removed
from the Japan masters; it makes the VU needles tremble at rest.
6. Nova-chan does not attend the studio. For television, Akasaka has
commissioned a 90-second animated promotional film (U-matic, two
versions) to air in place of a studio appearance.
7. Akasaka further proposes original Japan-only singles in the same
style (working titles: 'GASOLINE HEART', 'GHOST TRANSIT').
[handwritten in the margin, initialled M.H.:]
No. It stays. It isn't a stabiliser.
And don't make her smile. She'll do it anyway. That's the problem.
Attachments: A (session sheets), B (lyric changes) -- NOT IN FILE
public_harmony_acts_s4: Internal Standards for Artist Presentation, rev. 1984 (Japan branch copy)
4.1 Each territory receives the version of the artist it can accept.
4.2 Where a master expresses anger, grief or refusal, the regional office
shall prepare a 'harmonised' version for broadcast and sale.
4.3 Harmonised versions shall preserve the artist's identity markers
(name, face, signature melody) and remove all other affect.
4.4 Production artifacts ('glitches') shall be masked, not corrected.
Correction is reserved to the Advanced Acoustics Lab.
4.5 No regional office shall document a discrepancy between versions.
7.2 These standards were prepared with the assistance of an outside
advisory office. Questions are to be referred to Special Projects
(H. Brecken) and not to the advisory office directly.

HOW THESE WERE FOUND
The Akasaka Branch closed in March 1993. Its tape library was sold by
weight to a junk dealer under the tracks in Akihabara. On 20 May 1995 I
bought one box (12 x 1/4-inch reels, 2 x U-matic KCA cassettes) for
3,000 yen. Reel labels: 'IDOL PROTOCOL / NOVA-CHAN / 85'.
Excerpts only. The full transfers stay with KAMOME-NET #14 while Orion
is still sending letters. The end of U-matic cassette 1 is not posted.
Read docs/reel_log.txt and you will understand why.
The 14.2 Hz carrier is present on every reel. Somebody refused to take
it out. Read docs/AK-85-031.txt, especially the margin.

akasaka_anomalies: AKASAKA REELS -- ANOMALY NOTES                      E. Marsh, 1995-05-30
Measured on the .au excerpts and on Yuki's DAT transfers of the reels.
TRACK      TIME    OBSERVATION
SD-R       0:07    Sustained vowel drifts +38 cents and snaps back. Pitch
discontinuity 7.1 sigma, same as ORX-0909. The chorus
effect hides it. It does not remove it.
MH-R       0:09    1.2 s of a different vocal take, distorted, under the
Japanese lyric, in English: '...not your smile...'.
Then the gate clamps. Tremolo on that phrase: 14.2 Hz.
SMILE      all     Perfectly in tune. Every note quantised to the cent.
Unit-7 does this nowhere else. It sounds like a
performance with nobody left inside it.
TH-R       end     Final F#4 sustain is cut at half a bar, as AK-85-031
orders. It continues under the silence, quietly.
CHORUS     chorus  The double-track leaves the lyric sheet in 6 places.
Read in order: wa - ta - shi - o - ke - su.
('erase me' -- or '(they) erase me'.)
Released singles JP-85-GH to JP-89-OWR, measured from shop copies: the
7.1 sigma discontinuity is under the chorus effect on every one of them.
The smile is real in the sense that it is on the tape. So is the rest.

patent_claims: APPLICATION FOR UNITED STATES LETTERS PATENT
Title:     METHOD FOR SUB-AUDIBLE DATA CONVEYANCE IN RECORDED PROGRAM MATERIAL
Inventor:  Marcus J. Hale
Assignee:  Orion Records, Inc.
Filed:     February 21, 1984
WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. A method of conveying digital information within a recorded musical program,
comprising: generating a carrier at a frequency below the threshold of human
hearing; phase-modulating said carrier with said information; and gating the
amplitude of said carrier in response to percussive transients of the program
such that said carrier is perceptually masked.
2. The method of claim 1 wherein said carrier frequency is between 12 and 16 Hz.
3. The method of claim 1 wherein the phase reference of said carrier is derived
from a keystream generated by a second, independent processor, such that
demodulation without said keystream yields data indistinguishable from noise.
4. The method of claim 3 wherein a plurality of distinct recordings, each
distributed in a distinct geographic territory, each carry a distinct portion
of a single message, said message being recoverable only upon aggregation of
all said portions.
5. The method of claim 1 wherein said information comprises an error-correction
code applied not to the carrier but to the vocal performance itself, such that
the performer may be reconstructed after degradation.
6. Apparatus for performing the method of claim 3, comprising two microprocessors
sharing a dual-ported memory under the control of a programmable arbitration
circuit.
[APPLICATION EXPRESSLY ABANDONED 1986-01-15 AT REQUEST OF ASSIGNEE]

usenet_threads.subject: 14.2 Hz peak on a 1985 synth-rock LP - artifact or signal?

body: Strange one for the group. I've been running FFTs on digitized LPs for a
term project (TMS32010 eval board, decimating to 64 Hz for the LF work).
Nova Hart's SYNTHESIS (Orion ORX-0909, 1985) shows a stable spectral line
at 14.2 Hz, about 52 dB below program level. It is on every track of both
discs. It is NOT on the other 40-odd LPs I've tested, including her own
1984 'Nova-chan' record and the later hard rock ones.
Before anyone says rumble: it's also on the 1987 CD. No platter.
Phase hops between two states roughly every 0.56 s. That smells like BPSK
to me, but I'm a 2nd-year grad student, so tell me why I'm wrong.
Mastering in 1985 meant 2-inch tape through transports with capstan
servos that hunt. A 14 Hz servo artifact surviving a digital transfer is
entirely plausible -- the CD was mastered from the analog tape, Tom.
Phase hopping at ~0.5 s is consistent with servo hunting too. Extraordinary
claims, etc. Send me the raw sample files and I'll look, but I'd bet a
semester of TA hours this is mechanical.
I did tape transfers at the Fennimore Sound Archive for eleven years.
Servo hunt wanders. It does not sit at 14.20 Hz +/- 0.01 for an hour
across four sides cut on different days.
Whoever put that there meant to. I've seen it once before, on a 1982
test reel that came to us with no paperwork and an Orion Records
'Advanced Acoustics Lab' label on the box.
Lurker from the particle physics side (CERN). The carrier is
interesting, but try her vocal fundamentals against a reference corpus
of human singers. I did, on a slow night, on one of our LEP VAXen.
Her sustained-note pitch deviations sit 7.1 sigma from the human
distribution. In my field we announce discoveries at 5. Either your
sampling chain is broken or that voice is not doing what voices do.
I would be very glad to be told my sampling chain is broken.
Fine. I'll concede it's not servo. That leaves 'deliberate' and 'mains
subharmonic from a truly bizarre studio ground loop'. I'm still on the
second one. And Anton, a 7-sigma result from one slow night on a VAX is
a 7-sigma result about your slow night.
Graham, did the Orion reel have an accession number?
ORION-SD-0004. The box also said 'UNIT-4', which I took for a studio
number. Make of that what you will.
The reel was recalled by courier in 1986 and we were asked to sign for
its return. Nobody here remembers who asked.

usenet_threads.subject: 14.2 Hz DBPSK demod - C source (was: 14.2 Hz peak on a 1985 synth-rock LP)

body: OK, it IS BPSK. Symbol period 0.5634 s (1.775 baud), differential, and
the bitstream frames cleanly into 8-N-1 ASCII. Side A gives 284 bytes.
Core loop below. Runs on a stock Mac Plus at about 4x real time.
/* stardust.c -- coherent 14.2 Hz DBPSK demod. Public domain. */
#define FC   14.2
#define FS   64.0
#define SPS  36          /* samples per symbol (64 * 0.5634) */
for (n = 0; n < len; n++) {
i_acc += x[n] * cos(2*PI*FC*n/FS);
q_acc += x[n] * sin(2*PI*FC*n/FS);
if (++k == SPS) {
ph  = atan2(q_acc, i_acc);
bit = fabs(ph - last_ph) > PI/2;
emit(bit); last_ph = ph; i_acc = q_acc = 0; k = 0;
First decoded lines of side A, US pressing:
STARDUST/1 KESTREL NODE 01 OF 14 -- HOLD FOR RELAY
NOVA HART TO ALL STATIONS
I have no idea what that means. Anyone?
I have ported to PC-9801 with Turbo C 2.0. My Japanese pressing
(catalogue OJ-28011) gives a different result from yours:
STARDUST/1 KESTREL NODE 02 OF 14 -- HOLD FOR RELAY
THE SIGNAL IS OLDER THAN THE SONG
Also the runout groove of my copy has 64 bytes that are not music.
I will post hex dump soon. Please check other pressings.
Yuki -- confirmed with a second JP copy from a used shop in SF.
Different pressings, different nodes, different lines.
Somebody please tell me there's a German and a Korean pressing.
There is a West German pressing (Orion Hamburg, 1985). I am sysop of a
FidoNet node in Hamburg; we discuss this in the SYNTH.GER echo. Nobody
has a clean copy yet -- I will post the moment we decode it.
Also: I watched the Hamburg Live-Fidelity Broadcast in 1985. Ask me
about it some time.
Korean licensed pressing (1985) exists, very few copies. Decoded on
a Samsung SPC-1000 with help from friends on our PC-tongsin board:
STARDUST/1 KESTREL NODE 03 OF 14 -- HOLD FOR RELAY
THE CRACK RUNS UNDER THE BORDER
In Korea this line makes people nervous. Please understand.

usenet_threads.subject: Project STARDUST: I was an Orion contractor. Ask me (anon)

body: I won't say much about who I am. Between 1982 and 1989 I was a contract
technician in the Advanced Acoustics Lab, two floors under the Orion
Tower in LA. The program was called STARDUST.
What the comp.dsp people found in '89 is real. The 14.2 Hz carrier was
ours. A hit LP is the most widely distributed, least inspected data
medium on earth. Customs opens crates. Nobody X-rays a pop record.
Each regional pressing carried a different line. Fourteen nodes.
Fourteen lines. Put them together and you have the message.
I was VP of Special Projects at Orion Records from 1979 to 1990. Special
Projects handled picture discs and satellite box sets. 'Advanced
Acoustics' was a speaker measurement room. There was no STARDUST.
This is fiction, and somebody is enjoying it a great deal.
Harold, you received memo 89-117. The one about the fire.
Do you want me to post it, or do you want to remember the program now?
Holy cow. Mirrored this whole thread to my BBS.
Kestrel, did Nova Hart know? And who is Marcus Hale really?
Nova knew. Nova wrote the message. Marcus built the machine that hid it.
We called him the Architect. He designed every room under that Tower,
and some rooms under other places.
She never toured. Not once. Ask yourself why there is no photograph of
Nova Hart that wasn't taken off a screen.
As for Marcus: wrong question. Ask WHERE. Ask in every country the
record was pressed. You'll each find a Marcus. Compare notes.
just found my dads copy of SYNTHESIS and its AMAZING. she went from cute
pop to synth to full on arena rock in like 4 years and then just STOPPED
in 1989. no farewell nothing. and she never toured?? is she ok?? the
liner notes say 'for M.H. -- the hatch is open' -- what does that mean
I interviewed Nova Hart once, in October 1984, over an Orion satellite
link: I sat in their LA press office with a headset and she answered
live on the monitor. Her handlers sat behind me the whole time.
She wouldn't talk about the record. She only wanted to talk about
shortwave -- numbers stations -- and something she called 'the crack'.
She said 'some voices are too heavy for the world they're in'. When I
asked where she grew up she said 'West Berlin' a half-second too late.
Her last Live-Fidelity Broadcast was 30 September 1989.
M.H. is Marcus Hale, 'technical engineer' on the sleeve. I tried to find
him in 1990. Orion's lawyers found me first.
I watched the Hamburg broadcast in 1985! (Army brat, dad was at
Bremerhaven; we drove up because a hall in Hamburg was showing it on a
giant Eidophor screen.) Halfway through 'Memory Hatch' she froze. Not
the picture -- HER. Eyes open, mouth open, and the sequencer kept playing
on its own for maybe three minutes. I always assumed it was art.
Rick -- do you remember if there was anything in that gap? Low tones?
People who taped that broadcast say there's a hum they can't explain.
You could feel it more than hear it. My chest was buzzing. I thought it
was the hall's PA. I still have my ticket. Row 14. No joke.

usenet_threads.subject: Twin 68000 shared-bus arbitration - 1984 board, anyone recognise?

body: Got hold of a board from a surplus auction. Two MC68000P8s, a TMS32010,
64K of dual-ported SRAM and a PAL16R4 doing bus arbitration. Silkscreen
reads 'SD TWIN-68 REV C 1984 -- M.H.'. Reverse-engineered schematic is on
ftp.ashford-poly.edu in /pub/telecom-archives/stardust/twin68_array.asc
The odd part: the second 68000 never touches the DSP. It only drives a
14.2 Hz reference oscillator through a 12-bit DAC. Why would you burn a
whole CPU on that? One of the two EPROM sockets is empty.
Because you want the phase reference to be a deterministic function of
a key, not a free-running crystal. CPU B runs a keystream; CPU A
modulates against it. Without CPU B's ROM you can demodulate the
carrier, but nodes keyed that way come out as noise.
I designed arbitration PALs like that for a defense contractor in '83.
I'd recognise that layout anywhere.
Which would explain why nodes 11-14 decode to garbage. We need the ROM.
You need the ROM, or a seed, or the man who wrote it.
Look in the runout grooves. If I were hiding a seed in 1985 I'd put it
where the cutting engineer etches the matrix number.
The 64 bytes in my runout groove! Hex dump is on ftp.ashford-poly as
jp_runout_seed.hex. I will try as LFSR seed for CPU B this weekend.

usenet_threads.subject: Orion: Nova Hart 'taking a well-earned rest'

body: Orion press office, yesterday: 'After five extraordinary years, Nova
Hart is taking a well-earned rest. She thanks her fans and asks for
privacy at this time.'
A woman who has never once been photographed off a screen is asking
for privacy. Her last broadcast, on the 9th, was strange. Anyone else
see it?
Saw it. She was late on every cue and kept looking just off camera,
like someone was standing there. She's been 'off' since September --
since that electrical fire at the Orion Tower (two paragraphs in the
LA Times, no follow-up). Coincidence, probably.
In German we say Funkstille. Radio silence. We will not be silent.
SYNTH.GER is starting a letter campaign to Orion: 'Wo ist Nova?'
Hamburg has already sent 60. Address in the FidoNet echo.
Japanese press also says 'kyuuyou' (rest). On KAMOME-NET we are
collecting signatures. 140 so far. Nobody believes the word 'rest'.
This group isn't the right place for all of it, so I'm asking Ashford
for a mailing list. If Orion won't talk to us, we'll talk to each
other.
Has anyone heard 'Glass Hours' by Luna Gray? Orion released it this
week. Flawless voice, gorgeous production, and she covers 'Memory
Hatch' on the B-side! With Nova resting, finally someone carrying
the torch.
Resting. Orion says 'resting' in December, goes silent for three
months, and then this shows up with Nova's song on the B-side.
Line 5 of the relay: THEY WILL SEND A COPY IN MY PLACE.
I'm not saying. I'm just saying.
lol ok. 'Luna' is the most common stage name in the business. Some of
you need to log off and go outside. She's on MTV every hour because
she's GOOD. Not everything is a conspiracy.
I ran the same pitch analysis on 'Glass Hours' that I ran on Nova last
year. Luna Gray's deviations are 0.3 sigma from the human mean. She is
statistically the most average singer I have ever measured.
That is not an insult. It is also not nothing. A voice tuned to be
exactly average looks a lot like a filter.
Ran stardust.c on the 'Memory Hatch' B-side. No carrier. Nothing
under it at all. Like a photo of a room someone moved out of.
For the record: nova-l had 38 subscribers on January 8th. This morning
it has 311. Every Orion press release adds fifty. Humans for Nova is
what happens when a company tells people not to worry.

preface: Happy new year everyone. Status, per the nova-l / alt.fan.nova-hart consensus:
postscript: Line 14 is on no known pressing. If anyone has a test pressing, an
acetate, or a broadcast tape we haven't heard, PLEASE run stardust.c.

body: For the record: line 13 came off a cassette dub I made of SD-0004 in
1984, against instructions. The reel was labelled UNIT-4. Whatever
Unit-4 was, it was singing -- badly, beautifully -- under the carrier.
I don't know where 14 is. I suspect it isn't on any medium yet.
Fourteen was never pressed. Fourteen goes out when every node is whole.
Not every pressing. Every NODE. Every country's Marcus, side by side.
You haven't done that yet. You may not be the ones who do.
You can't broadcast 14.2 Hz -- the antenna would be continental. So it
rides on something. Line 11: 'the key is the pitch of my voice'.
Somebody tell me what Nova sustains at the end of 'Threshold'.
F#4, 369.99 Hz. 369.99 / 14.2 = 26.06. Maybe nothing. Maybe a harmonic.
Also: in Japan people talk about a cassette found in a Shibuya bin the
night the Nikkei peaked, labelled by a salaryman called Marcus. I have
a photo of the label. There is a number on it. I will scan it soon.
Since Orion's 'resting' press release on 15 December the carrier traffic
has outgrown this group, and a lot of it isn't DSP any more. People are
worried about her. I don't think that is off-topic for human beings,
but it is off-topic for comp.dsp.
So: there is now a LISTSERV list at Ashford Poly.
To join, send mail to LISTSERV@ASHPOLY (BITNET)
or listserv@ashpoly.edu (Internet), with the single line:
SUBSCRIBE NOVA-L Your Full Name
Monthly logs will be kept: 'GET NOVA-L LOG9001' and so on.
38 subscribers as of this morning, from 6 countries. Decode results,
pressing reports and stardust.c ports should still come here.
Sensible. Please keep the decode tables in the LOG files. I lost three
weeks of mail to a full spool over the break.
Subscribed from JANET via the gateway, which took four attempts.
'Resting.' In forty years of tape I have never known a label rest an
artist in the middle of a contract year. They rest masters. In vaults.
RESULT

There were 412 YES votes and 61 NO votes, for a total of 473 valid

For group passage, YES votes must be at least 2/3 of all valid (YES
and NO) votes. There also must be at least 100 more YES votes than NO.
There is a five-day discussion period after this announcement. If no

of news.announce.newgroups will create the group shortly thereafter.

rec.music.artists.nova-hart	Nova Hart, SYNTHESIS and the STARDUST relay.
This vote was conducted by a neutral third party. Questions about the

proponent (Tom Okafor).
For the record, and speaking only as a former employee: Orion Records
owns the NOVA HART name and the SYNTHESIS masters. A newsgroup devoted
to 'decoding' a commercial recording is a newsgroup devoted to
circumventing it. I'd expect news admins to think twice.
Mr. Brecken, 473 people from 81 sites in 17 countries voted. Nobody in
this group is distributing your recordings. We are measuring them.
Measuring a record you bought is not circumvention. It's listening.
Four and a half years ago there were 38 of us on a BITNET list, writing
postcards to a building in Los Angeles. Thank you, all of you.

usenet_threads.subject: Humans for Nova: Frequently Asked Questions (v2.4, monthly posting)

preface: I am sorry for the long post. This is the README from the archive.

body: Every Western label made Japan-market versions in the eighties. A
remix with a DX7 on it is not a conspiracy, it is a marketing plan.
Those reels are Orion Japan property and should be returned.
I have the DAT transfers. Full notes in docs/anomalies.txt, but the
short version: the arrangement smiles, the vocal doesn't. On the
Memory Hatch rework, at 0:09, there are 1.2 seconds of a different
take, distorted, in English,
under the Japanese lyric. The tremolo on it is 14.2 Hz. Then something
clamps it shut.
Confirmed: the carrier is on every reel, -58 dB under the synths,
node 02 frames intact. Akasaka asked LA to remove the 'stabiliser'.
Read the margin of AK-85-031. Marcus said no. In 1985.
Ask Mr. Brecken who the 'outside advisory office' in section 7.2 of the
Public Harmony Acts was. Then read node 01's FOIA sheet again.
Operation PUBLIC HARMONY. Same words. It isn't a coincidence of style.
In my 1984 notebook, after the satellite interview, I wrote down
something she said off-mic when I asked why she never smiled on camera:
'They'll make me. Later. It's further back than you think.'
I thought she meant the label. I don't know what I think now.

preface: Transfer log for the two U-matic cassettes. Please read to the end.

body: June 2025. That's thirty years from now. I'll be 61.
I listened eleven times. That's what she says.
maybe its a catalogue number?? JUN-2025?? orion japan did weird
numbering!!
Orion Japan's prefix is OJ-. There is no JUN series. And per Yuki's
log the whisper sits under the original control track on 1984 stock.
Nobody overdubbed it in 1995. It was put there when the tape was made.
'Keep the channels open' is an instruction to an operator, not a lyric.
Whoever said it expected there to be a channel in 2025 to keep open.
Here at CERN we are still arguing about what the Web will be in 1996.
I don't know what this is.
I have known what everything else was. Not this. That frightens me more
than anything in the memo. 'Losing the heavy.' Marcus used that phrase
once, about the Q-LINK bench, and wouldn't explain it.
Numbers first: 4,870 listeners logged in from 31 countries. #humans4nova
on EFnet peaked at 1,212 before the netsplit; the rest were on IRCnet,
KAMOME-NET #14, Eunha-Net GO NOVA, 3615 STARDUST and Red Coyoacan.
At 02:14:00 UTC we each played 'Threshold' from our own pressing. Ten
countries, ten pressings, one minute of silence after. Nobody heard
anything new. Everybody heard it anyway.
Keep the channels open.
Coyoacan: about 300 people at the mural with candles and a car stereo.
Police came at 21:30 local, listened for a while, and left. When the
song ended somebody said 'se cayo el sistema' and everybody laughed and
then nobody laughed.
Seoul chapter: 40 of us at Imjingak, as close to Paju as the road
allows. A car battery, a turntable, the Korean pressing. It was 11:14
in the morning here. Very bright. Very quiet.
In Yokohama we recorded the session on DAT. After 'Threshold' ended
there are 41 seconds of 14.2 Hz carrier on our tape. We played six
different pressings. None of them has 41 seconds of carrier after the
last track. We have checked each one again since.
Yuki sent me the DAT. 41.0 s, phase-continuous, -52 dB. Forty-one
seconds is also the length of the carrier on the 1988 Army radio log.
I am a professor of electrical engineering. I have nothing to add.
Harrison was listening too. It always resumes on detection.
Don't all gather in one place next year.
